subject: Follow-up: Hosting constraints & region availability for Fintech Inc PoC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Ng <olivia@fintechinc.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Quick recap & next steps — hosting constraints for PoC

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet you and hear more about the Fintech Inc PoC goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap from call:
- Primary constraint: EU data residency + regulatory controls for customer-identifiable data (PII).
- Business ask: start a 6-week PoC to validate inference accuracy, latency from EU and APAC users, and estimation of per-token costs.
- Procurement will require security artifacts (SOC2, DSAs/DPA, KMS controls) and a short hosting/residency statement.

High-level hosting options (we discussed):
1) Hosted (Redwood API) — fastest to start; we can pin requests to EU-only regions and route traffic within EU, but we need procurement to confirm contract controls (DPA + SCCs) are acceptable.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — single-tenant GPU pools in a region; predictable throughput and clearer data isolation than shared hosted endpoints.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — required if procurement mandates customer-managed networking or full control of keys and egress.

Questions for you (so we can scope technical deep-dive):
- Can procurement accept a hosted EU-region offering if we include a DPA and region-only routing in the SOW?
- Do you have a target latency SLA for APAC users (Singapore office)? Ballpark numbers (e.g., sub-200ms to your edge) will help us size options.
- Expected sustained QPS and average sequence length for the PoC (tokens per request).

Next steps I propose:
- Technical deep dive: schedule a 45-minute session next week with Marissa (solutions engineer) to review architecture and do a latency/region feasibility plan.
- Share procurement contacts and specific evidence requests so we can bundle the right artifacts.
- I attached a short region availability matrix to show current EU/APAC coverage and typical tradeoffs.

Avails for the deep-dive: Mon/Tue 9–12 EST or Wed 14–17 EST. Let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0143

Hi Ben,

Thanks — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side to help scope the PoC: 

Procurement/security constraints:
- Data residency is non-negotiable for customer PII: must remain in EU for storage and processing.
- Procurement will accept hosted if data processing and storage are guaranteed to occur within the EU region AND contractually enforced (DPA + SCCs or EU Addendum). We will confirm whether SCCs alone suffice or if we need an addendum.
- SOC2 report and a short note on key management (who holds keys, rotation, HSM options) will be required.

Latency expectations / users:
- Primary users are EU-based; APAC office (Singapore) will have occasional admin access. For the PoC we expect <250ms median round-trip from EU users. APAC is not critical but would like to understand typical tail latency if routed to EU.

PoC sizing (initial estimate):
- Expected concurrent requests: 5–10 sustained QPS during business hours.
- Typical prompt length: 120–250 tokens.
- We will provide a sample dataset (anonymized) after NDAs are in place.

Procurement contact: procurement@fintechinc.com — they will follow up with a checklist.

Next step: yes to the technical deep-dive. Tue 9–11 EST works for our engineering lead. Please include Marissa and Laura.

Cheers,
Olivia Ng
Head of Product — Fintech Inc
olivia@fintechinc.com

Subject: Re: Quick recap & next steps — hosting constraints for PoC

Thanks for the details, Olivia — very helpful. Looping in Marissa (solutions engineering) to run the deep-dive and Laura (enterprise sales lead) for procurement coordination.

Quick notes on tradeoffs based on the constraints you shared: 
- Hosted (EU region pinning): pros = fastest to get running, lowest initial ops; cons = you rely on our contractual controls (DPA + SCCs) and we still operate shared control plane (we can offer EU-only data plane and no export of payloads outside region for the PoC). Good fit if procurement accepts the DPA.
- Dedicated: pros = single-tenant GPU pool, clearer isolation and throughput guarantees; cons = requires commitment (monthly) and longer lead time to provision. Good if you need stable predictable latency and want Redwood-managed hardware but isolated tenancy.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): pros = full network control, customer-kept keys, and easiest to satisfy strict legal/regulatory asks; cons = highest ops overhead and longer setup timeline.

Given your QPS (~5–10) and token sizes, hosted or dedicated are both viable for a short PoC; private is likely overkill unless procurement requires customer-controlled networking or KMS. For APAC latency checks we can run synthetic tests from Singapore and provide percentile numbers.

Marissa — can you prepare: (1) a short comparison table (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC) tuned to Fintech Inc's QPS and token sizes; (2) a proposed test plan for EU & SG latency; (3) list of security artifacts and the format procurement prefers. I attached the region matrix I mentioned.

Olivia — I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 09:00 EST and lock the deep-dive.

Best,
Ben

Hi all — thanks for the context. I’ve put together a short technical plan and attached the comparison matrix and the SOC2 stub. Highlights / immediate asks: 

What we’ll deliver for the PoC (week 0–6):
- Week 0: contract addendum + DPA confirmation from procurement; exchange minimal NDAs.
- Week 1: baseline Hosted EU runbook (EU-only routing), synthetic latency tests (EU -> EU and SG -> EU) using a small sample workload you provide.
- Week 2–3: run PoC traffic with monitoring (latency p50/p95/p99, token counts, cost estimate).
- Week 4–6: iterate on model variant, configure batching/caching, and produce cost/latency report.

Information needed from Fintech Inc before the deep-dive:
- A sample (anonymized) set of typical prompts and average token sizes.
- Confirmation whether procurement will accept SCCs + DPA or needs an EU addendum.
- If possible, a contact for a network test point in Singapore (IP or a small curl-able endpoint) so we can run realistic measurements from our APAC edge.

Preliminary sizing recommendation based on stated QPS: start Hosted EU pinned instance with autoscaling and enable prefix caching. If procurement requires stronger isolation post-PoC, we can rapidly transition to Dedicated. For strict key control, we’ll discuss a VPC path with customer-managed KMS.

Attachments included:
- deployment_comparison_matrix.xlsx (detailed cost/latency/ops tradeoffs)
- SOC2_AICPA_report_stub.pdf (high level — full report available under NDA)
